chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Asbat who said:

Ibn Faddal asked Ibn Bukayr in the mosque, saying: 'What do you say about a woman who breastfed a boy for two years, then breastfed a girl for less than two years until the two years were completed? Does that invalidate the prohibition between them?' He said: 'It does not invalidate the prohibition between them, because it is breastfeeding after weaning. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "There is no breastfeeding after weaning." Meaning that when the boy or the girl has completed two years, they have exited the limit of milk, so it does not create a prohibition between him and anyone who drinks from her.' He said: 'And our companions say that it does not invalidate the prohibition unless the boy and the girl drink sip by sip.'
ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding a child for less than two years after the first child was weaned create a marital prohibition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia juristic consensus that breastfeeding after weaning (post-suckle) does not establish marital prohibition, based on the Prophet’s dictum 'no suckling after weaning.' It further refines the condition of direct consumption, noting that prohibitions arise only when the children drink directly from the breast, distinguishing this from indirect or sequential feeding. This ruling underscores the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the temporal and physical conditions of *radha'*.
